summary: Geshe Lhundub Sopa was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967, serving as Professor of South Asian Studies (attested 1987-1998).
Geshe Lobsang Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sera Monastery (attested 1980) and served as abbot at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987).

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921-2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he was attested in posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907-1990) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a post at Leiden University in 1960 and served at Drepung Monastery, including as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (attested 1987-1992, 2004).

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933-2013) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1970-1973). He served as a teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from around 1978 to 2013.

Geshe Tashi Tsering (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries. He held teaching posts at Kopan Monastery, Gandhi Foundation College, and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (1994).
Geshe Tsondru Namgyal is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He obtained Geshe degrees through his studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal (1901-1983) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery. He taught at Columbia University (~1967-1974) and worked at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center from circa 1958 to 1983.

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (born 1930) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held academic posts as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991 and from 2001 to 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926-1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938-1959) and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later teaching Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Gessho Sasaki (1875-1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from around 1896 to 1899 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1901 to 1926.

Giacomella Orofino is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977-1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982-1985) under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1992.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda (1888-1953) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as professeur adjoint at Kyoto University (1934-1948) and held a post at Rissho University.

Gikyo Ito (1909-1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and later held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and Kyoto Sangyo University.

Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1991-1998) and held posts at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and the Insight Meditation Center (~2001).

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar. In 2004, he was attested at the CNRS as a senior fellow, at EHESS as a member, and at FMSH directing the Indo-French social sciences exchange program.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin.
